title.en: Metres and centimetres (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en: How far is it between the two walls of the classroom? Children found it with steps, a rope and a metre tape.

A centimetre (cm) is a small unit. It is about the width of your finger.
A metre (m) is a bigger unit. A metre is a hundred centimetres, so 1 m = 100 cm.
We measure short things like a pencil in centimetres and long things like a room in metres.
To measure with a ruler, place the zero mark at one end of the object and read where the other end falls.
A tape measure is useful for longer lengths like the window or the classroom wall.
Find the distance between two walls. Different ways give different counts, so use a standard measure.

problem.en: A pencil is 15 cm long. A rope is 2 m long. Which is longer?

requiredIdeas.en: Line up the end of the object

points.en: Use cm for small things and m for long things.
